title: A Harbor for the Compass
premise: In 1919, Odile Almeida drives for suffragist Marguerite Voss and secretly reads the letters that pass through her hands, keeping a private ledger of the town's suppressed grievances. When the army requisitions the harbor town and seizes every official record, Odile realizes his hidden ledger is now the only surviving account of the soldiers' abuses and the officials who enabled them. Hunted by a captain determined to erase the record, Odile and an unlikely circle—the printer's widow, a deserter, and Marguerite herself—smuggle the truth into print before the victors' historians can write their version. The book ends with the pamphlet distributed across the country, Marguerite arrested but unbowed, and Odile finally stepping out of invisibility to sign his name as witness.
about_author: Tamsin Nakamura is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated letters in municipal collections, where she first encountered the marginalia of ordinary people caught in official histories. She writes historical fiction about the records that almost didn't survive.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sealed Envelopes
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. We meet him steaming open letters in the Voss household, memorizing which grievances to pass along and which silences protect people—until army trucks roll into the harbor and Captain Renard announces the requisition of all civic records. Odile hides his ledger inside the spare tire well as soldiers search the house. Emotional beat: the quiet dread of a man whose careful invisibility is ending.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Remembers
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, with interludes from the ledger itself. He discovers the seized records include testimony he helped collect; a young dockworker's sister begs him for help, forcing him to choose between safety and witness. He recruits the printer's widow Céline and the deserter Anselme, forming a fragile found family around the hidden book. Emotional beat: guilt transforming into resolve.

chapters.title: Ninety-Six Hours
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Odile and Captain Renard, who suspects the ledger exists and takes Marguerite hostage to draw it out. The climax: Odile trades himself for her at the print shop, while Céline runs the press through the night and Anselme holds the door. Renard burns the shop, but the pamphlets are already on the morning train. Emotional beat: sacrifice, terror, and the cost of being seen.

chapters.title: A Name on the Record
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, weeks later. The pamphlet circulates nationally; Renard is recalled under inquiry, though justice remains partial. Marguerite, released pending trial, refuses to flee. In the final scene, Odile walks into the inquiry hall and signs the witness register in full view—no longer a driver, no longer invisible—with Céline and Anselme beside him. Emotional beat: hard-won belonging and the claim that truth needs names attached.
